What’s not so great is that even though this app is advertised to function on three platforms, iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, it’s impossible to log into the Apple TV app. I created and account with the “sign in with Apple” option, bought an annual subscription, and created full login credentials.

On the Apple TV app, two options for access are presented. The simplest (which works well for other apps I use) is the “restore subscription” option. This is supposed to simply recognize that my signed-in Apple ID already has a subscription purchased via my iPhone, and install the same credentials on the Apple TV app. Try this, and it does nothing. The other option is to login with your Guitar Tricks username and password. Try this, and it says the credentials are invalid.

I submitted a help request to the Guitar Tricks “contact support” option in the iPhone app, and never got a response. 

So, two stars for some good lessons, but no more than that for one of three platforms being inaccessible, and zero response from customer help.

Progress is something that is clunky in the website. It takes a few steps to get there. It’s even harder on the app. 

It’s not tracked up front on the app. You have it. It’s there. It is just hard to find. 

In the lessons area every time you log on it looks as if you have done nothing. So if you don’t recall where you were you waist time looking around.

But I do hope they work out a more graphic based or flow chart style of tracking progress. It helps motivate when you see ALL you have accomplished. And discouraging when it looks like nothing.

No matter which one I use, the app or the website, it should be easier to pickup where you left off. Each chapter has 6 or 8 lessons, and each lesson has multiple sections. I’m not usually able to complete all parts of a lesson in one sitting, and that’s where returning to where you left off because a hassle. Other training software I use takes me make to exactly where I left off.If there is a lesson or practice exercise you want to return to you can’t mark it as a favorite on the app, but you can on the website. Guitar Tricks Is Great, the App is Lacking. I subscribed to Guitar Tricks to supplement my in-person guitar lessons that I’ve been taking. These lessons do a great job and add another element of review for me. It is also great to relax from the in-person training I am doing and just learn a song here and there. Using the program on-line is great, however, using the program on my iPad or iPhone leaves a lot to be desired. The two things that make the app almost useless are the inability to use multiple panes and the non-existence of the auto scroll as you are playing along in the lesson. I am a beginner and having to try to play guitar and then move the music every 5 seconds renders the app useless to me. I am not a good enough player to do this, if I was, I wouldn’t need the app or Guitar Tricks at all. To the first point, it is great that you see the instructor, but i want to see lyrics and the tabs as well and I’d like to be able to make all of these views dynamic (e.g. scrolling with the song, ability to loop, etc). Final thought, I have read other reviews that have mentioned that the app is confusing to navigate. I completely agree with this sentiment. Finding where you are in the lesson track is not possible in the app. They have link to the last “lesson” that you’ve watched, but that could be anything, a song you were toying with, an old lessons, a tutorial on some guitar maintenance. I started watching the lessons on my iPad at the beginning, only to realize that i skipped a bunch of lessons because there was no clear way to see what lesson I should complete next.

As noted above, this review is just for the app not Guitar Tricks overall. I’ve been a member for 2 months and have been satisfied with the system.

Was great until they killed live Group Lessons. April 5th, 2020 Review [UPDATE]

Much better. I’ve added a star to my previous review, the iPad GT app has been updated and addresses one of my major complaints as we can now finally SEARCH their massive song library (still boggles the mind how basic functionality was overlooked). 

Resizeable tablature and backing tracks remain elusive. 

FWIW, I still firmly believe the guitar instructional marketplace is ripe for interactive group lessons. They do have a top instructor now offering the service on a limited basis as an independent service, but not to scale. 

 -
Feb 1st, 2019 Guitar Tricks pulled the rug out from their loyal paying customers by eliminating their Full Access Plus service. It offered 6 hours a week (3 sessions two hours each) for $39 a month flat fee, taught by the fantastic instructors they feature in their video tutorials. 

I made more progress in a year than the previous ten on my own, but can’t help feeling sour that they pulled the plug ending the best thing they had going for them. Fortunately for me a competitor now offers live webcam sessions plus Live Studio courses. Sorry had to get that off my chest. 

This review is intended for feedback on the app, not the service. While the website is feature-packed and great, the iOS apps seem to be mere afterthoughts, simply repurposing their video library and repackaging assets for mobile. 

AppleTV and iPad apps have the screen real estate to be something special, but lack so many necessary features, so instead of playing guitar where it’s convenient for the user, you’re forced to play near your computer (which might have been fine in 1998 when they started, but severely dated two decades later). 

3 biggest oversights using Guitar Tricks app 

GT boasts a library [now over] 1,000 songs (!), yet AppleTV / iPad has NO SONG SEARCH. 3 years ago they added _SORT_ by Popularity, Alphabetical title, Difficulty, alpha Artist, Style, Newest, and Instructor, but no search Artist nor Song. Scroll scroll scroll for days before giving up. 

On-screen Tablature is NOT resizeable, tiny text requires you take your hands off guitar and screenshot so you can zoom, before you exit back to the lesson. Incredibly Inefficient. 

Jam Tracks and Backing Tracks are on the site, but NOT in iOS. Most users hit up JamPlay or YouTube to satisfy their needs. 

Minor quibble, they do have a scrub bar to slow-down videos so you may play along with the instructor, but it does not list if it’s 50%, 75%, or 90% like the website, leading to random tempos from eyeballing it. 

I feel iOS apps are not a priority there, paying customers receive maybe a feature update or two annually, plus bug fixes, but GT developers continue to fall behind the competition, failing to innovate. 

It’s my wish they would let another dev firm prototype an app to management, and design a true iOS app designed from the ground up for mobile, using the same excellent video lessons into something more usable. 

If you don’t mind playing guitar by your computer, the service offers considerable value.

Some instructors spend too much time talking about theory and other things mixed right in with the middle of the song instruction, irrelevant to actually learning the song, and then fly way to rapidly though the chords, progressions and riffs, making learning difficult and multiple rewinds and replays necessary. The theory may be interesting , but should come in separate sections, NOT in the middle of trying to learn to play a part of the song. Songs should be broken down into smaller sections for learning , or have ability to mark and loop sub-sections so you can repeat as needed. 

On the plus side, transcriptions and techniques are generally good, except for songs with multiple guitars in the original . “Just play guitar 1” is a cop out. There are usually very good ways of combining multiple parts for solo.

The teachers and clarity are a Game changer. Let’s be honest. Everyone thinks they are a great teacher but few are. I’ve tried guitar lessons on and off for the 22 years I’ve been trying to learn guitar. In the end, messing about and learning through trial and error has always been more fun and I’ve ditched the teacher.

The app is easy to use - yes it sometimes has glitches. Yes it sometimes is easy to lose track. But structure isn’t what keeps my interest. This app is addictive because the lessons are clear, they are short, they let you jam before boredom kicks. You feel like you are winning. Constantly.

The teachers aren’t arrogant. The clips are short which means if (like me) you occasionally zone out...you can go back and watch that but again.

Brilliant. I actually learn and like it!

One massive glaring omission. The app is ok, I chose this over Fender Play but not sure that was the right decision. The authentication is different between the website and the app, so if you register on the website with google or Facebook, you can’t login to the app the same way. 

The biggest issue however is once in the app, there is no easy way to track your progress - so when you go back to the app your have to delve around in history to find out what you have done - and to add additional confusion, the lessons in the history are named individually, but in the progress section you have to choose a lesson group, so have to guess which lesson group your last individual lesson was in. 

The website version has progress bars on the lessons, this is all that is needed, but for the app to be missing these it makes it clunky just to do something basic like pick up where you left off, seems like a really basic omission for what should be a learning application.

Simple and perfect for beginners. I don’t often write reviews but Guitar Tricks seems worthy of the praise. I’m a beginner who started with JamPlay last year but soon got lost in to many options with various teachers, and their app was not as good as the website which is never a good thing.

Back into learning again this year and Guitar Tricks seem to have it nailed. The app is simple to use and the learning route and quality has improved my playing great already. The tutors are straight to the point and everything you watch is genuinely useful with no padding. 

The app sometimes suffers from videos failing to load after being open a while on my iPad Pro but a restart always fixes it. That’s the only improvement I’d make.
